source_title: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Consistent Nachiket Bhute emerges as Vidarbha’s pace lead - Sportstar
source_excerpt:
Nachiket Bhute recently represented India-A against Australia-A in two unofficial Tests. | Photo Credit: PTI
Having found themselves in an early predicament midway through the first session, Abhinav Tejrana and Lalit Yadav had made a fine fist of digging Goa out of a hole on the first day of its Ranji Trophy 2026-27 match against Vidarbha at the VCA Jamtha Stadium in Nagpur.
Brought together at 35 for four, the pair batted over 100 balls to get to the Lunch break, and with the new ball seen off, seemed well-set to keep going. Then within a matter of overs, all of their good work was undone.
First to depart was Tejrana, punished for flirting with a delivery in the channel, soon followed by Lalit, who was victim of one that crashed into his front pad.
The architect of both their downfalls was the same, Nachiket Bhute, the tall 26-year-old who has slowly emerged as a leader in this Vidarbha attack.
Against Goa, he would claim five wickets in the first innings, showing immaculate control over his line and length with both the new and old balls, and forcing batters to manufacture mistakes on a wicket without substantial sideways movement.
“There was a little bit of moisture in the air, so I knew that if I put the new ball in the right areas I would get purchase,” Bhute reflected on his spell after the match. “My aim was to get the ball as close to the stumps as possible, and to make the batters play as much as possible.”
Together with India international Yash Thakur, IPL star Praful Hinge, and Rajneesh Gurbani, Bhute has formed part of a well-rounded and threatening pace bowling group for the side.
He noted that the group has a very tight bond, and is always keen to support each other.
“We have a very strong bond, we keep helping each other,” he said. “Whoever is bowling will always pass on information to the rest. That’s always helpful to the individual, it means that you don’t need an over or two to get set, you’re set from the very beginning.”
He reserved praise for the veteran Gurbani, who has returned to Vidarbha after a stint with Maharashtra, and credited his advice for helping him create the wicket of Snehal Kautankar caught behind.
“ Bhaiyya is a great swing bowler, so he keeps telling me about batters. For that wicket, he noticed that his front leg wasn’t coming out as much, so he advised me to push it fuller,” he said.
Nachiket Bhute had picked 29 wickets in seven games in the Ranji Trophy last season. | Photo Credit: Periasamy M.
He also pointed to his learnings from Yash, who has made his national team debuts in both white-ball formats, saying, “He’s an X-factor for our team since he hits 140+kmph on a consistent basis. He will keep talking to me about how to preserve my body, when to keep the intensity high, and when to keep it low.”
Bhute enjoyed a breakout season for Vidarbha in 2025-26, claiming 29 wickets in seven matches at an average of 18.10, and he has begun this season in impressive form again, scalping 14 wickets at 14.28.
Those displays last season even earned him a call-up to the India A set-up for its recent red-ball matches against Australia A in Puducherry, where he claimed the wickets of internationals Peter Handscomb and Josh Phillipe, and hung around with the bat alongside Vidarbha statement Hinge to help India A rescue a draw in the dying embers of the day.
“It was a great experience, it was a little bit new for me. There was a lot for me to take away from the coaching staff, about bowling and about the game, that I want to implement in this season,” he said.
“Playing in Puducherry, conditions were very different, so Bala sir (head coach Lakshmipathy Balaji) was telling me about using the conditions in my favour and doing everything I can to help my bowling.”
However, while his recent performances have been impressive, Bhute was clear that he would only look to follow the process behind them without getting caught up in the outcome as he said, “I’ll take the positives from that season, but I follow a process and don’t think about anything extra. When I’m bowling, I just focus on the ball and I focus on my areas.”
